system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
PHYSICS CHECK
Governing physical relation: Fatigue crack propagation rate (Paris' law: da/dN = C(ΔK)^m). Inner-race spalling initiates as a surface crack that propagates under cyclic loading. The early-stage propagation produces subtle, high-frequency vibration components that increase in magnitude as the crack grows. The challenge is detecting these changes within the existing sensor bandwidth and logging constraints.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Signal processing module (software implementation on existing PLC or edge device)
2. Root mean square (RMS) calculation of high-frequency vibration envelope (300-900 Hz band)
3. Trend analysis algorithm tracking the rate of change of RMS values over rolling 7-day windows
4. Threshold comparison logic with configurable hysteresis
5. SCADA integration for alarm output
All components use existing infrastructure except for the software implementation, which requires development.

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY
Standard practice relies on overall vibration amplitude alarms, which typically trigger too late. This solution uses the same sensor and logging infrastructure but adds software processing. Implementation burden is minimal (software-only), operability matches existing procedures, and maintenance is reduced by extending bearing life. Cost class is significantly lower than adding specialized vibration analysis hardware or replacing bearings on fixed schedules.

EXECUTABLE TEST
1. Protocol: Install the algorithm on 20 identical fan drives with known bearing histories. Collect vibration data at 1 kHz and log processed values at 1 Hz for 12 months. Record all actual bearing replacements and false alarms.
2. Instruments: Existing 1 kHz vibration sensors, SCADA system, and a separate high-speed data acquisition system for validation.
3. Pass/fail thresholds: Must detect all bearing replacements at least 14 days before failure; must not exceed 2 false alarms per year across all 20 units.
4. Duration: 12 months of continuous operation to capture seasonal variations and multiple bearing life cycles.

DESIGN/INDICATOR: Rate of change of RMS vibration in the 300-900 Hz band over a 7-day rolling window
THRESHOLD: 0.15 dB/day increase for 3 consecutive days
TEST: As described above in EXECUTABLE TEST section
